tables.title: Blob use steps for scalar multiplication (CCOP = 0b10000001)
tables.text_helper: Table 193, "Blob use steps for scalar multiplication (CCOP = 0b10000001)", in section 25.5.3 (ECC scalar multiplication) on page 764. Columns: OPSTEP, MODE in PKA, GCMPH in SAES, Coupling or chaining operations, End-step event(1), CPU action. 8 data row(s). Notes: 1. The application must clear and/or perform described event for CCB to automatically go to the next step.; 2. SAES cannot be used for any operations, for security reasons.

rows:
– Enable the PKA in the correct mode, writing in PKA_CR 
MODE= 0x20 and EN=1 (repeat if EN bit stays clear). 
Wait for INITOK=1 in PKA_SR.
– Optionally, decrypt blob encryption key in the SAES, 
using DHUK in 256-bit wrapped key mode.
– Set up AES-GCM in decryption mode with DHUK or the 
decrypted key in register (if applicable).
– Write input point P coordinates in the PKA RAM. When 
computing a public key, write basepoint G coordinates.

– Complete GCM initialization in decryption mode, using 
saved random IV.
– Write reference tag in CBB_REFTAGR.

Write ECC scalar multiplication parameters in the PKA 
RAM, clearing CCF flags in the SAES, triggered after 
each 64-bit write.

– Write encrypted k in SAES_DINR, and runs AES 
decryption round.
– Write incrementally scalar multiplier k in the PKA, using 
0xCCB magic number. 
– Repeat for each 16 bytes block of data.

– Complete GCM final.
– Read computed tag in the SAES (returns 0).

Start the operation in PKA setting START bit in PKA_CR.
Do not use SAES during this step (under reset).

The PKA computes the operation. The PKA RAM is read 
as 0.

Read kP point coordinates in the PKA RAM. If this point 
is the public key verify it matches the reference public key 
computed in Table192 before saving the created blob in 
non-volatile memory.
notes: 1. The application must clear and/or perform described event for CCB to automatically go to the next step.
2. SAES cannot be used for any operations, for security reasons.
